analysis.evidence: הָאִשָּׁה is the subject of וַתֵּרֶא. The following words כִּי טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל give the content of her perception: she saw that the tree was good for food.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה, “the woman saw,” הָאִשָּׁה names the subject of the feminine singular verb. The later לְאִישָׁהּ, “to her husband,” expresses the marital relationship.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: After וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה ‘the woman saw’, כִּי introduces what she saw, namely that the tree was good for food (טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל).
analysis.morphology: Unprefixed, unsuffixed subordinating conjunction.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: In כִּי טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל, טוֹב agrees with הָעֵץ, “the tree,” and לְמַאֲכָל specifies what the woman judged it good for: food.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively.
analysis.sense: good in quality, fine, fit for use

analysis.evidence: In טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל, the woman sees that the tree is good for food. She then takes מִפִּרְיוֹ, “some of its fruit,” identifying the referent as a fruit-bearing tree.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל means “the tree was good for food.” The woman then takes some of its fruit and eats it.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition לְ + masculine singular absolute noun מַאֲכָל.

draft.change: Clarify the existing Gen.3.6 citation under ki-that by identifying the role of the second כִּי.
draft.definition: After a verb of perception, כִּי introduces what is perceived.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.6 the repeated כִּי introduces a second clause governed by וַתֵּרֶא, and the prefixed וְ coordinates it with the first.

analysis.evidence: וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה ‘the woman saw’ governs both clauses. After ‘that the tree was good for food’, וְ joins a second observation, and כִּי introduces its content, תַאֲוָה הוּא לָעֵינַיִם ‘it was a delight to the eyes’.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ ‘and’ + uninflected subordinating conjunction כִּי ‘that’.
analysis.sense: Introduces the content of what is seen.

analysis.evidence: In תַאֲוָה הוּא לָעֵינַיִם, the pronoun הוּא refers to the tree. The woman sees that the tree itself is “a delight to the eyes,” so the noun denotes the object of desire.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וְכִי תַאֲוָה הוּא לָעֵינַיִם, “and that it was a delight to the eyes,” הוּא refers back to the masculine singular הָעֵץ, “the tree.” The feminine noun תַאֲוָה, “a delight,” is the predicate.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person masculine singular.

analysis.evidence: וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה describes the woman looking at the tree. In תַאֲוָה הוּא לָעֵינַיִם, the eyes are the organs through which she finds the tree visually appealing. The following לְהַשְׂכִּיל expresses the appeal of gaining insight.
analysis.morphology: Common-gender noun, dual absolute, with prefixed לְ and the definite article.

analysis.evidence: נֶחְמָד agrees with הָעֵץ, “the tree.” The following לְהַשְׂכִּיל specifies what made the tree desirable to the woman: the prospect of gaining wisdom.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a Niphal participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively.

analysis.evidence: In וְנֶחְמָד הָעֵץ לְהַשְׂכִּיל, the woman sees the tree as desirable for gaining wisdom. מִפִּרְיוֹ (‘from its fruit’) confirms that the noun refers to a fruit-bearing tree.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In וְנֶחְמָד הָעֵץ לְהַשְׂכִּיל, the infinitive gives the woman's reason for finding the tree desirable. She sees eating its fruit as a way to gain wisdom.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ of purpose

analysis.evidence: The subject is הָאִשָּׁה, the woman. The partitive phrase מִפִּרְיוֹ specifies what she took, some of the tree’s fruit, and וַתֹּאכַל tells what she did next, she ate it.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The woman sees that הָעֵץ, “the tree,” is good for food. וַתִּקַּח מִפִּרְיוֹ וַתֹּאכַל says that she took some of its fruit and ate.
analysis.morphology: Partitive preposition מִן with assimilated נ + masculine singular construct noun + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ referring to הָעֵץ.

analysis.evidence: וַתִּקַּח מִפִּרְיוֹ means “she took some of its fruit.” The following feminine singular וַתֹּאכַל keeps הָאִשָּׁה (“the woman”) as its subject, with the fruit understood as what she ate.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The woman gives some of the fruit she took (מִפִּרְיוֹ). לְאִישָׁהּ identifies her husband as the recipient, and וַיֹּאכַל says that he ate it.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: give something to someone for their use

analysis.evidence: After the woman takes the fruit and eats, גַּם introduces לְאִישָׁהּ in וַתִּתֵּן גַּם לְאִישָׁהּ, “she gave some to her husband too.” The closing וַיֹּאכַל, “and he ate,” confirms that he too shared in the fruit.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected additive particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The woman (הָאִשָּׁה) is the subject of וַתִּתֵּן ‘she gave’. The suffix in לְאִישָׁהּ refers to her and identifies the recipient as her husband. עִמָּהּ ‘with her’ describes his presence.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ ‘to’ + masculine singular construct noun אִישׁ + third-person feminine singular possessive suffix ־ָהּ ‘her’.

analysis.evidence: The woman takes fruit and gives some to her husband (לְאִישָׁהּ). The masculine singular וַיֹּאכַל identifies him as the one who eats the fruit.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
